Subject: Order form redlines — clarification on training & feedback license

Hi Samir / Atlas legal team,

Thanks for sending over v3 of the order form redlines this morning. A couple of items popped up that I wanted to flag early so we can avoid a back-and-forth later in your procurement review:

1) Training / model learning carveout — your redline removes the training exception language and replaces it with a narrow analytics-rights clause. Our engineering and product teams are concerned because that change would prevent us from using customer feedback (even aggregated signals) for model improvements unless you separately agree. Can you confirm whether Atlas intends to allow Redwood to use non-personally-identifiable feedback for model quality improvements?

2) Feedback license scope — the redline remains ambiguous on whether the feedback license is perpetual and sublicensable to service providers (eg. inference partners, SRE vendors). We propose: feedback license limited to improving Redwood services, non-sublicensable except to subcontractors under NDA, and not to be used to train 3rd-party commercial models.

3) Output ownership carveouts — your team asked for "customer ownership of output" language. Our standard is to grant customers rights to use outputs for their business while retaining model weights and derivative training rights with Redwood (subject to the feedback license scope above). If you need specific attribution or an escrow requirement, please spell that out and we can loop in legal.

I attached our suggested redlines and a short one-pager that maps each requested Atlas change to our standard position (see "redwood_feedback_license_draft.docx" and "Atlas_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf").

Next steps: if Atlas can confirm the desired scope for feedback (use for Redwood model improvement vs. broader training rights), I can get legal to produce a tracked-change order form for signature. Happy to jump on a quick call with your legal/ procurement and our GC if that helps move faster.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — clarification on training & feedback license

Vanessa —

Appreciate the quick summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Atlas is open to Redwood using aggregated, de-identified feedback for internal service improvements, but we want express language that prohibits training of general-purpose models that could be commercialized outside the Redwood-Atlas relationship.

- We need the feedback license to be perpetual for auditability purposes, but we can consider a limited sublicense model (eg. Redwood may share with vendors only to the extent necessary to deliver the service and under the same restrictions).

- Regarding output ownership, Procurement wants explicit "Customer owns outputs" language since downstream teams will be storing and using generated content. Legal flagged that phrase as broad; they proposed a narrower operational use grant instead.

I'll leave the exact wording to legal, but please have your GC provide suggested tracked changes that reflect (1) de-id-only training, (2) no commercial 3rd-party model training, and (3) permissible subcontractor access. We can then run it through our internal compliance check.

Samir
Director, Data Strategy — Atlas Retail
samir.rao@atlasretail.com

Thanks Samir — that scope works as a starting point. I discussed with product and our GC this morning and we can propose the following compromise in tracked changes:

- Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified customer feedback and telemetry to improve Redwood services. This use explicitly excludes training of models for resale or commercial distribution to unrelated third parties.

- Feedback license is granted in perpetuity to Redwood, but sublicensing permitted only to subcontractors that are bound by confidentiality and the same usage restrictions.

- Output: Customer is granted a license to use outputs for internal business operations and to distribute them to third parties for their business purposes; Redwood retains ownership of model weights and derivative rights for the service, subject to the limitations above.

I've uploaded a tracked-change order form to the DocuSign link below for your legal team to review. If Atlas wants to add an escrow or additional audit right we can surface that to finance and legal for evaluation, but it will likely affect pricing.

Proposed next step: legal reviews our tracked changes and we schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call tomorrow afternoon. Karthik / Neha — please advise if the wording above has any red flags from your side.

Best,
Vanessa
